pl-l4d1c1-d1e115.summary: Takes up the Samaritan image: approaching the wounded man, he applied the bandages of the sacraments to heal him, since God instituted the remedies of the sacraments against the wounds of original and actual sin.
claims: The sacraments are God's remedies for original and actual sin.

pl-l4d1c1-d1e118.summary: Sets four initial questions: what a sacrament is, why it was instituted, in what it consists and is performed, and what difference there is between the sacraments of the old and new law.

pl-l4d1c1.summary: Opens the treatise on the sacraments with the parable of the Samaritan, who bound the wounded man's wounds: God instituted the sacraments as remedies against the wounds of original and actual sin. Four questions come first: what a sacrament is, why it was instituted, in what it consists and is performed, and how the sacraments of the old and new law differ.
claims: God instituted the sacraments as remedies against original and actual sin.
The treatise first asks what a sacrament is, why it was instituted, in what it consists, and how old and new sacraments differ.
